clue.text: Negotiator gets the password wrong

indicators.note: getting the password wrong means its letters come out in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A bargainer flunks the security check by mistyping the password.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges the eleven letters of THE PASSWORD.
explanation.definitionFit: A union representative elected by workers bargains with management on their behalf, so is a negotiator.

clue.text: Some of the athletes in preliminary race

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few of the runners are competing in a qualifying round.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'in preliminary race' as the definition; 'in' is only a link, since the noun alone substitutes for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A qualifying round decides who goes through to the final, the usual athletics sense.

clue.text: Initially partner was irritated, being chucked

indicators.note: Initially asks for just the opening letter of the word partner

parts.note: to have itched is to have been irritated by an urge to scratch

explanation.surface: Someone's partner got cross on being dumped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link; the definition is 'chucked' in the sense of thrown.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw a ball, as in cricket or baseball, is to pitch or chuck it.

clue.text: Lake — see sailor heading north

indicators.note: the sailor is heading towards north, so that letter comes after him

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Look at the lake: a seaman is making for the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is a link; in a down clue 'heading north' could suggest a reversal, but the pieces simply run in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mountain lake, especially in the north of England, is called by this name.

clue.text: Day when gun is carried in London area

indicators.note: the gun is carried inside the day's abbreviation, so one goes within the other

parts.note: WED is short for Wednesday, a day of the week
the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: On a certain day a firearm is brought into a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sten was a cheap British submachine gun of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The theatre and shopping district of central London goes by this name.

clue.text: Harangue worker after end of labour

indicators.note: after places the insect worker behind the letter taken from labour
end of asks for only the final letter of the word labour

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's standard worker, from the worker ants of a colony

explanation.surface: A labourer is berated once the job is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To harangue is to lecture loudly and angrily, the same as a tirade or rant.

clue.text: Designer finds fault with implement, leading to depression

indicators.note: leading to means the first pieces come before the final piece

parts.note: a chip is a small flaw or defect in china or glass
a pen is a writing implement
a dale is a valley, a dip in the land

explanation.surface: A designer complains about a tool, which gets him down.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Chippendale was the celebrated eighteenth-century English furniture designer; 'finds' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Chippendale was an English cabinet-maker whose furniture designs gave a style its name.

clue.text: Female performer — I chant, doing a maths exercise

parts.note: an actor is a stage performer
to chant is to sing in a monotone

explanation.surface: An actress chants away while working through her homework sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking a number or expression into its multiplying components is a classic algebra or arithmetic task.

clue.text: Subordinate worker who won't get taken for a ride?

definitions.text: who won't get taken for a ride?

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a lowly worker carrying out orders, and literally an infantryman, who marches instead of riding a horse.

clue.text: Reason we will put down for gathering movement

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece is put down below the first

parts.note: grounds are the reason or justification for something
we will contracts to we'll, written without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: We will record our reason for joining a growing campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link; 'put down' places WE'LL beneath GROUNDS in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A swell of public opinion that builds steadily is a mass movement gathering strength.

clue.text: Enormous shop there — my park is ruined

indicators.note: ruined says the letters of the words before it are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A complaint that a giant store has spoilt the speaker's local park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges the letters of THERE and MY PARK; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A very large out-of-town supermarket is the biggest kind of retail store.

clue.text: Noise one doesn't give if not bothered

definitions.text: Noise one doesn't give if not bothered

parts.words: Noise one doesn't give if not bothered
parts.note: plays on the idiom for indifference: someone who doesn't care is said not to give a certain owl's cry

explanation.definitionFit: The cry of an owl figures in the idiom 'not give a ...', meaning not care at all.

clue.text: Weight system in old city

explanation.definitionFit: A system of weights used for precious metals shares its name with the ancient city besieged by the Greeks.

clue.text: Less significant fit of temper before row

indicators.note: before puts the fit of temper ahead of the row

parts.note: a pet is an old word for a sulk or fit of pique
a tier is a row of seats

explanation.surface: A minor tantrum precedes a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with 'cow' on the surface but here is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Something more petty is smaller and more trivial than another.

clue.text: Split, like a vehicle in motion losing its front

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter, its front

parts.note: a car in motion is being driven

explanation.surface: Something is torn apart like a speeding car shedding its bonnet.
explanation.definitionFit: Riven is the old past participle of rive, meaning torn or cleft apart.

clue.text: Some men, thus excited, wax lyrical

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Several men, worked up like this, start to gush.
explanation.definitionFit: To wax lyrical is to speak with great eagerness and passion about something.

clue.text: Weird emanation's beginning to descend on lake

indicators.note: in a down clue the first letter descends from above onto the lake
beginning asks for the opening letter of the word emanation

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: A ghostly vapour starts to settle over a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncanny and unsettling is strange in a spooky way.

clue.text: Big noise and little man had food and drink

parts.note: a din is a loud racket
Ed is a short form of Edward, a man's name

explanation.surface: A loud fellow and a small one shared a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big noise' looks like a VIP but is a literal loud noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To dine is to eat a meal, usually with drink, especially in the evening.

clue.text: Hesitation when meeting big Greek god

indicators.note: meeting puts the hesitation next to the size abbreviation

parts.note: er is the sound of someone hesitating
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: Someone falters on encountering a mighty Greek deity.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of love is the counterpart of the Roman Cupid.

clue.text: A mother's boy

parts.note: a dam is a mother, especially of an animal

explanation.surface: A mother's son.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is part of the possessive surface; the definition is 'boy', a boy's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A male first name, belonging to the first man in Genesis.

clue.text: Brown salt water — very good for drinking!

indicators.note: the salt water takes in the other piece, as a drinker takes in liquid

parts.note: the sea is salt water
PI is short for pious, very good in crossword language

explanation.surface: A remark that brown seawater is excellent to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddish-brown pigment from cuttlefish ink gives its name to the colour of old photographs.

clue.text: Able to pay out for a chemical

explanation.definitionFit: Being able to meet one's debts is to be solvent; a liquid that dissolves other substances is the chemical sense.

clue.text: A peculiarly sombre saint

indicators.note: peculiarly means arranged in an odd way, so the letters of sombre are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A holy man strangely gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A peculiarly sombre' reads as a description of the saint, but 'peculiarly' signals a rearrangement of the word that follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: St Ambrose was a fourth-century bishop of Milan and one of the Doctors of the Church.

clue.text: Ineffectual person has gone mad, showing deep resentment

parts.note: a dud is a failure or useless person

indicators.note: mad tells us the letters of gone have gone wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A useless man has lost his mind and is visibly bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges GONE to GEON; 'has' and 'showing' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in high dudgeon is to feel indignant offence.

clue.text: English politician to be in debt to queen giving sanction

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
to owe is to be in debt
R is for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: An English MP owes money to the monarch, giving official approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction an action is to authorise it, giving someone the power to do it.

clue.text: Right name given at end of story

indicators.note: given at end of places the name abbreviation after the story

parts.note: a story is a fib or lie

explanation.surface: A character's name appears at the close of the tale, by right.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, a right to keep someone's property until a debt is paid is this kind of claim.

clue.text: Sea captain has upset little old fellows

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word for fellows upside down

parts.note: fellows are men
O is the short form, little version, of old

explanation.surface: A ship's master has knocked over some small elderly men.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain of the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne's Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea.

clue.text: Look after seaman in port

indicators.note: after puts the word for look behind the seaman

parts.note: OS is an ordinary seaman
lo is an old exclamation meaning look

explanation.surface: Look after a sailor in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look after' seems to mean 'care for', but 'after' only sets the sailor first; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Norway is a seaport on a fjord.

clue.text: Participant in boat race puffed audibly

indicators.note: audibly says the word for puffed is heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: puffed is blew, as of the wind

explanation.surface: An Oxford or Cambridge rower panted noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is an Oxford or Cambridge student who represents the university, as in the annual Boat Race.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowers in the Oxford-Cambridge Boat Race earn a university sporting award named after a colour.

clue.text: Prevents from entering pub rooms

explanation.definitionFit: To bar someone is to keep them out; a pub's drinking rooms are called its public and saloon bars.

clue.text: Sort of hymn — carol is seen to be different

indicators.note: the letters of carol is seen are made to be different, so are rearranged

explanation.surface: A carol turns out to be an unusual kind of hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be different' rearranges CAROL IS SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn sung as clergy and choir leave the church after a service.

clue.text: Disagreement continued with travellers to end of day

parts.note: rovers are wanderers or travellers

indicators.note: end of asks for only the final letter of the word day

explanation.surface: An argument with wanderers kept going until nightfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A prolonged public dispute is a heated argument.
